source_text: Ἰγνάτιος, ὁ καὶ Θεοφόρος, ἠγαπημένῃ θεῷ, πατρὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐκκλησίᾳ ἁγίᾳ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Τράλλεσιν τῆς Ἀσίας, ἐκλεκτῇ καὶ ἀξιοθέῳ, εἰρηνευούσῃ ἐν σαρκὶ καὶ πνεύματι τῷ πάθει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῆς ἐλπίδος ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ εἰς αὐτὸν ἀναστάσει: ἣν καὶ ἀσπάζομαι ἐν τῷ πληρώματι ἐν ἀποστολικῷ χαρακτῆρι καὶ εὔχομαι πλεῖστα χαίρειν.
thought_title: Greeting to the Church in Tralles
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Tralles with a formal greeting, identifying himself and blessing the church.
pass_a_gloss: Ignatius, the [one] also [called] God-bearer, to [the one] beloved by God, [the] Father of Jesus Christ, [the] holy church that is in Tralles of Asia, chosen and worthy of God, being at peace in flesh and spirit by the passion of Jesus Christ, of our hope in the resurrection to him: whom also I greet in the fullness in apostolic character and I pray [her] to rejoice greatly.

choices.why: The name is a title meaning 'God-bearer'; rendering it as a name alone would lose the wordplay Ignatius uses of himself.
The dative θεῷ marks the agent of the perfect passive participle; 'beloved by God' keeps the passive force and the agent explicit.
The compound adjective means 'worthy of God'; 'worthy of God' preserves the compound sense without inventing a new English word.

choices.english: being at peace in flesh and spirit
choices.why: The participle is present active, describing the church's ongoing state; 'being at peace' keeps the durative force and the two spheres explicit.

choices.english: by the passion of Jesus Christ
choices.why: The glossary fixes πάθος as 'passion'; the dative is instrumental, so 'by the passion' marks the means of the peace.
The phrase describes the manner of greeting; 'in apostolic character' keeps the noun χαρακτήρ as 'character' and the adjective as 'apostolic'.

pass_b_english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, to the holy church in Tralles of Asia, beloved by God the Father of Jesus Christ, chosen and worthy of God, at peace in flesh and spirit through the passion of Jesus Christ, who is our hope in the resurrection to him. I greet her in the fullness, in apostolic character, and I pray that she may rejoice greatly.

last_rejected.quote: which is beloved by God the Father of Jesus Christ
last_rejected.why: Dative 'beloved to God' modifies the church; 'God' and 'Father' are in apposition, both dative, not 'beloved by God the Father'.
last_rejected.fix: beloved of God the Father of Jesus Christ
last_rejected.ruling: ἠγαπημένῃ θεῷ, πατρὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ uses dative of agent, meaning ‘beloved by God the Father of Jesus Christ’, which the translation conveys.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening address by making the recipient explicit and smoothing the sentence flow while preserving every claim and title.

notes.why: Capitalization varies for the same title; readers may miss that it is the same designation.

problems.why: Same epithet rendered four ways; reader may think these are different titles or people.
problems.fix: Standardize to one spelling, note 'Theophorus' as Greek equivalent.

problems.quote: Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus
problems.why: Same Greek title, one translated and one transliterated; reader may think they differ.
problems.fix: Use 'God-Bearer (Theophorus)' consistently or translate both the same way.

fixed: Standardized 'God-bearer' to 'God-Bearer' to match the consistent rendering of the epithet; the source uses the same Greek term (Θεοφόρος) throughout, so a single spelling is appropriate. The second problem refers to a different section not present in this excerpt, so no edit was needed here.
